title: Arithmetic and geometric Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Four Frobenius maps are attached to it.

1. The *arithmetic Frobenius* (Frobenius substitution) $\varphi_q\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, $z\mapsto z^q$, and the *geometric Frobenius* $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ [def-weil-frobenius-substitution].

2. For a $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the *geometric Frobenius automorphism*

$$
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):Y\longrightarrow Y,
$$

the base change [def-pc-base-change] of $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ along the $k_0$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] ($\gamma$ fixes $k_0$). It is an automorphism of the scheme $Y$ over $k_0$, with inverse $\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_q)$ by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ and of the fibre product; it is in general not a $k$-morphism (the empty scheme is an exception) but lies over $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ (it is semilinear). On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subseteq Y_0$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes\gamma(b)$ on $A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$.

3. The *absolute $q$-power Frobenius* $\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_Y:Y\to Y$ (identity on the space, $g\mapsto g^q$ on $\mathcal O_Y$) [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme].

4. The *relative Frobenius* $F_Y=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k:Y\to Y$, a $k$-morphism [def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber].

The maps $g_Y$, $\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_Y$ and $F_Y$ are three distinct endomorphisms of $Y$ in general. Convention: every Frobenius operator in this blueprint is induced by $g_Y$ and is geometric (Deligne's 'action of the geometric Frobenius $F\in\operatorname{Gal}(\bar{\mathbf F}/\mathbf F_q)$', $\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times F$).

split_report.summary: Checked against Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7) p.150-151, (1.1.8) p.151 and (1.1.14) p.153 (Deligne defines the Frobenius substitution, its inverse the geometric Frobenius, the Frobenius endomorphism F of X deduced from x -> x^q on X_0, and id x F as the geometric Frobenius action; he does not define the absolute Frobenius, taken from Stacks 03SM). Rewrote the statement to define all four maps the convention uses (arithmetic/geometric Frobenius of k, g_Y, absolute q-Frobenius, relative Frobenius F_Y), adding the affine description and inverse of g_Y; the old statement mentioned the absolute Frobenius only to contrast it and did not mention F_Y. Replaced stmt_dep def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties (an imported bundle) by def-weil-finite-type-morphism, the only property used, and added def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-pc-base-change, def-weil-affine-spectrum. New nodes: def-weil-frobenius-substitution (Mathlib leaf FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic), def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme and def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber (unsplit; Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry has no Frobenius at all). Did not point to def-trf-scheme-frobenius / prop-trf-frobenius-factorization (sec-six-functors), which define Phi = F_Y and the factorization Fr = g_sigma Phi, because def-trf-scheme-frobenius depends on this item (cycle).

statement_change.what: The unqualified claim that g_Y is not a k-morphism is false when Y₀ is the empty finite-type k₀-scheme. Then Y is empty and its unique endomorphism is over every base. Qualify only that remark by in general, explicitly allowing the empty scheme. The construction id × Spec(γ), its inverse, and its semilinearity equation are unchanged.

blueprint_update.statement:
For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the
arithmetic Frobenius of $k$ is

$$
 \varphi_q:k\longrightarrow k,
 \qquad z\longmapsto z^q.
$$

Put $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}$. For a finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, set
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and define the associated semilinear automorphism

$$
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\longrightarrow Y.
$$

This is distinct from the absolute $q$-power morphism of $Y$.
